thread:
support_elena: customer reports streaming responses cut off mid-token when traffic goes through Cloudflare -> ALB -> our origin. client reconnects and sometimes receives a resumed chunk (duplicate tokens) or an empty reconnect. seen ~20% of long-lived streams (>30s idle). req id: req_8f3b2a. billing spike for that customer after retries :grimacing:

morgan_product: ouch. how many customers impacted and do we have account/account id?

support_elena: just this customer escalated (acct-acme-42) but looking at logs it's sporadic across a few tenants behind the same ALB. timeline: starts fine, ~15s silent period, then origin emits final chunk and TCP close, client sees truncated payload and re-requests. attached example curl below.

support_elena: ```bash

curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \\  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?req=req_8f3b2a"
```

support_elena: client saw partial tokens up to chunk-22, then nothing. when client reconnected it requested same req id and our system treated it as a new session and billed tokens again (duplicate charge).

cloudflare_bot: alert: edge-keepalive-term-count increased x3 for host api.redwood.example in last 6h (rule: edge/keepalive-terminate).

ingrid_sre: this matches ALB idle/keepalive termination or Cloudflare proactively resetting origin connections. two axes to validate: (1) check ALB target group idle timeout (default 60s for ALB, NLB passthrough differs) and per-target connection reuse; (2) verify if Cloudflare is using HTTP/2 to the origin and doing connection coalescing + early FIN on idle streams. also confirm whether any intermediate LBs are doing connection drain during ASG events.

devex_ian: quick mitigations to try with customer:
- enable small heartbeat in server stream (e.g. comment-line SSE ":\n" every 10s) to prevent silence hitting edge timeouts
- set ALB idle timeout to >= 120s or switch to NLB TCP passthrough for streaming workloads
- consider forcing HTTP/1.1 between CF and origin (turn off http2) so chunk flush semantics are simpler

devex_ian: sample heartbeat we can add to quickstart:
```js
// send a SSE comment every 10s to keep proxies from marking connection idle
setInterval(() => { res.write(": heartbeat\n\n"); }, 10000);
```

morgan_product: do we have a billing-side dedupe we can apply for short reconnections? e.g., if same x-request-id reconnects within 30s, mark as resumed and avoid double-charge.

ingrid_sre: yeah we should. but first replicate reliably. can we get a pcap around one of these failures? tcpdump on the origin host while hitting the repro might show whether origin FIN arrives before the last chunk bytes leave the kernel.

support_elena: attaching two files to the thread: tcpdump-req_8f3b2a.pcap (uploaded to ticket) and nginx/access+error snippets.

devex_ian: another thing — ALB sends a FIN to idle targets during connection reuse; if the origin's kernel hasn't flushed the last chunk (due to buffering in our runtime), the FIN race can drop the trailing bytes. adding an explicit flush on Write or toggling socket linger can help.

ingrid_sre: plan: (1) repro locally with Cloudflare disabled (direct to ALB) and cloudflare-enabled to confirm difference, (2) try NLB passthrough to check whether TCP passthrough fixes it, (3) patch quickstart to include recommended heartbeat and origin-side flush. I'll take task and coordinate with infra to bump ALB idle timeout for a test target group.
